title: WPMS/309/2006 of RAGHUBIR SINGH and ORS Vs A.C.R.C and ORS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 309 (M/S) of 2006
Raghubir Singh and others ......Petitioners
Versus
Additional Chief Revenue Commissioner
and others ...... Respondents.
Present:
Mr. Lokendra Dobhal, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. H.S. Rawal, Advocate holding brief of Mr. V.B.S. Negi and Mr. Rajendra
Kotiyal, Advocates for the respondent Nos. 5 and 6.
Mr. Gajendra Tripathi, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
Dated: 21st July, 2017
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.

Heard Mr. Lokendra Dobhal, learned counsel for the
petitioner and Mr. H.S. Rawal, learned Counsel holding brief
of Mr. V.B.S. Negi and Mr. Rajendra Kotiyal, Advocates for
the respondent Nos. 5 and 6.
The respondents have instituted a Suit, being Suit No.
33 of 1997, invoking Section 176 read with Section 178 of the
U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, wherein,
the respondents to the suit sought to settle their share to the
extent of 1/3 share in relation to the property laying Khasra
No. 4/7, having an area of 3-80 acres, Mauja Ramnagar
Danda, Tehsil Parwadoon, District Dehradun.
The basis of the claim of the respondents plaintiffs was
that they claimed their right and title being the son of Tara
Singh. After the suit was entertained, the petitioners who
were defendant in the suit, notices were issued to them and
they filed their written statement on 22nd January, 1998. In
the written statement, in para 9, they have specifically
pleaded, that according to the family chart, Tara Singh died

2
issueless and his wife Sukhdei solemnized second marriage
with one Mr. Pratap Singh. It was the case of the petitioners
that the respondents who have claimed themselves to be the
son of Tara Singh was absolutely wrong and mis-conceived
and, thus, they were not entitled for any share devolving on
the basis of the succession their the predecessor Kaliya. In
support of his contention, the learned counsel for the
petitioner has placed reliance on the voters list, in which,
Sukhdei has been shown to be wife of Pratap Singh and not
of Tara Singh.
Be as it may. This fact about the family tree was not
categorically denied by the respondents in their replication
filed to the writ statement. The Court of Assistant Collector,
by the impugned order dated 28th May, 2001, had decreed
the suit of the respondent and, thereby, holding them to be
entitled to have 1/3 share devolved on them. Surprisingly,
the basis for rendering the judgment dated 29th May, 2001,
was under the premise that the petitioners have not filed
their written statement. This fact is absolutely contrary and
erroneous to the record because as per the pleading in the
writ petition, the written statement was already filed on 22nd
January, 1998, and that is why, it seems that the Court under
misconception, despite the written statement being on
record, did not frame any issue and the suit has been
decreed on this limited grounds that the written statement
has not been filed.
The petitioners, being aggrieved against the said order,
had preferred an Appeal before the Assistant Commissioner
(Administration), being Appeal No. 7 of 2002-03. In the
appeal, yet again, petitioners have reiterated almost an

3
identical stand which they have taken in their written
statement.
The Court of Additional Commissioner
(Administration) by the judgment dated 22nd September,
2003, has got tangent in recording that the statement of
Shyam Lal ought to have been recorded at the relevant time
before decreeing the suit.
This issue was not at all opened before him, the reason
being, the Assistant Collector has decided the suit under
Section 176 / 178, on the premise that the written statement
has not been filed by the petitioners. If that be so, obviously,
the Assistant Collector has not framed any issue and there
was no procedural necessity too to frame issue if no written
statement was filed, and once no issue was framed, there
was no occasion for producing any witness for adjudication
of the suit in the merit, or for recording their statements.
Thus, the finding recorded even by the Court of
Additional Commissioner about the inability of petitioners
to produce Shyam Lal for recording his statement is
erroneous and beyond the issue which was before the
appellant Court.
Being aggrieved by this order, the petitioners
preferred Second Appeal and the Second Appeal has been
decided by the judgment dated 6th August, 2004.
Surprisingly, the Court of Additional Chief Revenue
Commissioner, too, has recorded the perverse findings
which cannot be accepted by this Court. When the Second
Appeal was pending, during the intervening period, one of
the opposite party, namely, Munshi Singh, who was
opposite party No. 2, in second appeal, met with the said
demise. For the reasons best known to the petitioners, even

4
before the Second Appellate Court, petitioners have not
substitute the heirs of Munshi Singh at that particular point
of time when the Second Appeal was pending consideration
before the Additional Chief Revenue Commissioner.
However, before the Appellate Court, they have filed
an application for seeking an adjournment for bringing the
fact on record that since Munshi Singh has expired on 10th
September, 2001, hence, his heirs were supposed to be made
as a party in the Second Appeal by way of substitution. The
Second Appellate Court, in the operative portion of the
order, held as under :-
"While rejecting the adjournment application, has
consigned the second appeal, itself, on records."
It is established preposition of law that if one of the
parties to the dispute dies during the pendency of the
litigation, and, in any event, if the appellant or the plaintiff
fails to substitution heirs within a time prescribed under the
law and there are other co-defendant or co-respondent in the
suit or in appeal, then, in that event, the suit or appeal will
not abate qua the other contesting parties who are already on
record.
Order 22 Rule 2 deals with the situation where there
are more plaintiffs or defendants than one and if any one
dies, right to sue survives against surviving defendants or
defendant alone, suit has to proceed against at the instance
of plaintiffs or against surviving defendant or defendants.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Municipal
Board, Lucknow Vs. Pannalal Bhargava andothers, repored
in AIR 1976 SC 1091, has held in paragraph 5 as under :-
"5. We are however, unable to agree that the
question of abatement in this case would arise in view of
the fact that even if the suit had been dismissed against

5
defendant 5, the defendants 1 to 3 could individually be
sued for tendering accounts and for recovery of the
amount due from them. Whether they would be
ultimately found by the Court to be liable for the
plaintiff's claim is a different matter and will be decided
in the suit. There is, therefore, no substance in the plea
that the appeal as a whole has abated on account of the
death of Mohd. Yusuf."
Hence, the judgment of the Second Appellate Court
dated 6th August, 2004, abating the Second appeal as a whole
against the other co-respondents was bad and untenable and
he ought to have permitted the appellant atleast to press his
arguments in relation to his claim against the other surviving
respondents who were their on record on the Second
Appeal.
For the reasons stated, the writ petition is allowed. The
impugned orders are quashed. The matter is remitted back
to the Court of Assistant Collector to decide the Suit, being
Suit No. 33 of 1997, Shamsher Singh and another Vs. Munshi
Singh and others, after considering the written statements
which are already on record and framing the issues and
letting the parties to lead their respective evidence
exclusively on merits.
However, it is made clear that on account of
procedural anomaly committed by the Court below, this
Court has exercised its supervisory jurisdiction under Article
227 of the Constitution of India for quashing the impugned
orders. Any finding recorded above will not be treated as to
be the findings on merit inter se between the parties.
Writ petition is allowed and the matter is remanded
back to Assistant Collector to decide Suit afresh.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
21.07.2017
Shiv
